solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Briefly look at rivet

indicators.note: briefly asks for the word to be cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to look at something closely is to study it

explanation.surface: A quick glance at a metal fastener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' takes the last letter off STUDY.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a metal fastener, much like a rivet, driven through material to hold it.

clue.text: More emotional row grabs attention

indicators.note: grabs means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: An argument that draws notice becomes more emotional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a quarrel; it is a line of seats, TIER, which 'grabs' EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tearier is closer to crying, so more emotional.

clue.text: Some spirit needed to put on a show

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky or other spirit

explanation.surface: An actor needs a nip of whisky before putting on a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play or theatrical production, a show on stage or screen.

clue.text: Defect isn't in makeup

parts.note: a warp is a distortion or flaw
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A cosmetics product is claimed to be flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Face paint applied before battle, by extension any heavy cosmetics, is a kind of makeup.

clue.text: Court with outstanding officials, primarily

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A law court staffed by excellent officials.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to woo them, seeking their affection.

clue.text: Compensate for first of redundancies, with me busier, somehow

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the next word
somehow suggests the letters are rearranged in some way

explanation.surface: Pay off staff made redundant, with the speaker now overworked.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimburse is to repay someone for money spent, compensating them.

clue.text: After a party, a mother is a state!

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A mum declares herself in a state after a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a condition of distress; it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the states of the USA, in the Deep South.

clue.text: Old Scandinavian feature inspiring reverence at first

indicators.note: inspiring, literally breathing in, means one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: the nose is a facial feature

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word before

explanation.surface: An aspect of Viking culture that once commanded awe.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse is the language and people of medieval Scandinavia.

clue.text: A Romanic, twirly sort of pasta

indicators.note: twirly suggests the letters being spun round into a new order

explanation.surface: A Romance-language type of pasta that twists, like spaghetti on a fork.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a tube-shaped Italian pasta, so one example of the food.

clue.text: Race around some land

indicators.note: around suggests the letters being moved about into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Running laps round a plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of area, so it names a measured piece of ground.

clue.text: Opera star sending a short recording back

indicators.note: sending, paired with back, tells us to turn the letters round
back, with sending, means the pieces are read in reverse
short means the word is clipped to its familiar abbreviation

parts.note: a video is a recording

explanation.surface: A soprano posts a little clip of herself in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' clips VIDEO to VID; 'sending ... back' turns A + VID (AVID) round.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, a prima donna.

clue.text: Getting into fights, naughty child shakes

indicators.note: getting into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: vies means competes or fights
a brat is a naughty child

explanation.surface: A badly behaved kid joins a scrap and ends up shaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting into fights' reads as the child brawling, but 'Getting into' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To vibrate is to move rapidly to and fro, which is what something that shakes does.

clue.text: North American city initially ushering in vehicle insurance

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: insurance cover

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A city whose motor insurers first brought in new policies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ushering in' looks like one phrase; 'initially' takes U, and 'in' puts it inside COVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver is a major port city in British Columbia, Canada.

clue.text: Dirty child staggering around, edges away

indicators.note: edges away means the outermost letters at each end are removed

parts.note: lurching is moving unsteadily, staggering about

explanation.surface: A grubby kid tottering about, then sidling off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edges away' strips the L and G from the two ends of LURCHING.
explanation.definitionFit: An urchin is a scruffy, often mischievous street child, typically grubby.

clue.text: Translating Flemish, that man in the mirror?

indicators.note: translating turns one form of words into another, so the letters are recast

explanation.surface: A Flemish speaker, put into another language, looks at his reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun is what a man sees reflected: his own self.

clue.text: So — are you sure?

definitions.meaning: so in the sense of very or truly, as in 'so good'
an exclamation of surprise or doubt, like 'is that so?'

explanation.surface: Someone responds to news with doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means truly or very, and on its own it serves as an incredulous query.

clue.text: Allow change of scene after short story

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first
short means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a lie is a story, a fib

indicators.note: change of means the letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A permitted switch of setting after a brief tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts LIE to LI; 'change of' rearranges SCENE as CENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To license something is to permit or authorise it officially.

clue.text: Yellow bloom, particular flower

parts.note: prim means fussy or particular about propriety
a rose is a flower

explanation.surface: A yellow flower described as one specific type of bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring wildflower common in British hedgerows.

clue.text: Villain, topping accent!

indicators.note: topping means cutting the top, the first letter in a down clue

parts.note: a brogue is an Irish or Scottish accent

explanation.surface: A baddie exclaims how excellent an accent is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' reads as British slang for excellent, but it means remove the top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest scoundrel, a villain.

clue.text: Horse cut

definitions.meaning: a riding horse for hire or an ordinary nag

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hired riding horse and to chop roughly with an axe or blade.

clue.text: Conspire to devise an opening

definitions.meaning: to plot or contrive, as a scheme
a door or trapdoor in a deck or wall

explanation.surface: Plotters planning a way in.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to plot a scheme in secret; the other is a small door or trapdoor.

clue.text: Nothing good with respect to giant

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
re means concerning or with respect to

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on how good a giant is.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore an ogre is a man-eating giant.

clue.text: Extremely confident, jumping over

definitions.meaning: leaping over something with hands or a pole

explanation.surface: A cocky athlete hurdling an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes overweening ambition, and the verb form describes leaping over a bar or horse.

clue.text: Toughest part — that's horrible!

indicators.note: part says only a piece of the word is used

explanation.surface: Someone reaching the hardest bit of a task groans.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection expresses disgust, like 'yuck'.

clue.text: Group just out of the medals, we hear, began journey

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: we hear means a word sounding like the one described is wanted

parts.note: coming fourth means just missing the bronze medal

explanation.surface: A team that just missed the podium heads off on its travels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' swaps FOURTH, the place just outside the medals, for its sound-alike FORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out on a trip is to embark, so the phrasal verb means started travelling.

clue.text: Weeds found in Idaho especially

indicators.note: found in says the letters lie within the following words

explanation.surface: Weeds that particularly grow in the US state of Idaho.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weeds' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoe a bed is to clear it of unwanted plants with a garden tool.
